sections.description:
EMPLOYEES' OLD-GE BENEFITS (BOARD OF TRUSTEES) RULES, 1977
EMPLOYEES' OLD-GE BENEFITS (BOARD OF TRUSTEES) RULES, 1977
(Gaz. of Pak. Extr. Pt. II,. May 20. 1977
p. 849.)
[S. R. O. 438 (1)/77‑Islamabad,
the l2th May, 1977‑‑Rules framed by the Federal Government in
exercise of the powers conferred by section 44 of the Employees' Old‑Age
Benefits Act, 1976 (XIV of 1976).
1. Short title anal commencement.‑These rules may be called
the Employees Old‑Age Benefits (Board of Trustees) Rules, 1977.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. Definitions.‑In these rules, unless there is anything
repugnant in the subject or context,‑
(a) Act" means the
Employees' Old‑Age Benefits Act, 1976 (XIV of 1976) ; ,
(b) Institution" means the
State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan nominated under section 5 ;
(c) "Chairman" means
the Chairman of the Board ;
(d) meeting" means a
meeting of the Board ;
(e) section" means a
section of the Act ; and
(f) words and expressions used
but not defined in these rules shall have the meanings assigned to them
respectively in the Act.
3. Terms of office of members.‑‑(1) Members appointed
under clause (is) of sub‑section (1) of section 7 shall hold office
during the pleasure of the Federal Government and the members appointed under
clause (c) of the said sub‑section (1) shall hold office during the
pleasure of the Provincial Government concerned.
(2) Members appointed tinder
clauses (d) and (e) of sub‑section (1) of section 7 shall hold office for
the term of two years, aril each, such mem ber shall continue to hold office
after the expiry of his term until his successor is appointed and shall be
eligible for re‑appointment.
(3) A casual vacancy in the
membership of the Board shall be filled by nomination by the Federal Government
and the member nominated to fill such vacancy shell hold office for the
unexpired term of office of his predecessor or the period of absence, but not
beyond the date of expiry of tile term.
(3) A member shall cease to be
member if he absents himself from three consecutive meetings of the Board
without leave of absence from the Chairman or, in the absence of the Chairman,
of the Federal Government.
(5) A member appointed tinder
clause (b) or clause (c) of sub‑section (1) of section 7 may, by writing
under his band addressed to the Govern ment which he represents, resign his
office.
(6) A, member appointed under
clause (d), clause (e) or clause (f) of sub‑section (1) of section 7 may,
by writing under his hand addressed to the Chairman, resign his office.
(7) No act or proceeding of the
Board shall be invalid merely on the ground of the existence of any vacancy in.
or any defect in the constitution of the Board.
4. Procedure for appointment of members under clauses (d) and (e) of
sub‑section (1) of section 7 of the Act.‑(1) The Federal
Government shall, in consultation with the Provincial Governments, publish in
the, official Gazette two lists showing separately the organizations of
employers and insured persons recognized for the purpose of submitting names
from which members to be appointed under clauses (d) and (e) of sub‑section
(1) of section 7 shall be chosen.
(2) Within on month of the
publication of the lists under sub‑rule (1), every organization included
in the list may submit to the Federal Government the name of a person whom it
desires to be considered for appointment, where such organisation is of
employers, as a representative of employers, and where such organisation is of
insured persons, as representative of such persons, together with a summary of
the qualifica tions of that person.
(3) The Federal Government shall
consider the names submitted to it under sub‑rule (2) and shall, from
such names, select four persons to represent the employers and four persons to
represent the insured persons and shall published their names in the official
Gazette.
(4) If any member dies, resigns
or becomes disqualified under rule 5, the Federal Government shall notify the
